1. Sources

2. Tools

For tools.md (corpus tools, in קולות-היום-יום/):

  • kol_tools.py (the corpus tool; config UNITS = one entry per text, by project): units; data UNIT [FROM [TO]] (the translator's line data: label, transliteration, normalization, lemmas + ORACC morph, the rank-3 translation; for the proverbs the proverb numbers and ETCSL's translation per proverb); fill FILE (replaces each `@` transliteration placeholder by the exact base line – drafting with @ removed every retyping mismatch); verify [UNIT|PROJECT …] [--strict] (coverage and order against the base text, transliteration = base, the reserved and gated Hebrew strings licensed by the line's transliteration + normalization + lemmas (word-start anchored), the name traps, the formulas (the letter formulas in their line-shapes, niĝ₂-gig, giri₁₇-zal-še₃ nu-il₂, 5.5.1's "signs"), identical source lines with different Hebrew, and translation.rtl.md = the > lines); build PROJECT (the clean translation from translation--intro.rtl.md + the > lines, unit and section headings, proverb numbers, footnotes from the הערת שוליים bullets); grep (PROJECT|all|every) '<regex>' (the > lines of this corpus / of all corpora, with the transliteration); lookup '<regex>' (how the earlier corpora rendered a word, by transliteration/normalization).
  • build_parallels_index.py: python3 -I build_parallels_index.py [--stats] – parallels-index.md generated from the הקבלה bullets of all annotated files (one row per Bible reference, with the nearest echo tag and the quoted words), grouped by book with the Song of Songs, Proverbs and Qohelet first; the hand-written key findings above the marker line are kept on rebuild. (Unlike the earlier corpora's builders it needs no per-project parallels tables.)
  • Not committed (scratch, could become generic tools): a key-lemma consistency check (for each key lemma, the lines where it occurs without its fixed Hebrew) and a converter of `quote`, Book ch:v into the checkable `quote` (Book ch:v) form.

3. Guidelines

§6.7, one bullet:

  • Everyday-voices corpus (קולות-היום-יום/renderings.md, 2026-10-21): the Song of Songs' vocabulary is reserved and gated by script (דּוֹד only dādu, גַּן only kirû / kiri₆, תַּפּוּחַ, יוֹנָה, כַּלָּה ★, צְחוֹק only ṣīḫtu / ṣiāḫu, אָחַז only aḫāzu [cognate] – ṣabātu = תָּפַס here, a deviation from Gilgameš; שִׁיר, שׁוֹשַׁנָּה, לְבָנוֹן, מוֹר, פְּרִי (Akkadian) never); ṣawāru = צַוָּאר [cognate], sāqu = שׁוֹק, warādu = יָרַד, tamû D = הִשְׁבִּיעַ; mēlulu = שִׂחֵק; qadištu קְדֵשָׁה, nadītu נָדִיתוּ, kezertu כְּזֵרָה, batultu בְּתוּלָה; the incantation closing šiptum ul yâtu, šipat DN = הקסם אינו שלי: קסם DN. Sumerian proverbs: niĝ₂-gen₆-na = נְכוֹנָה (ETCSL "righteousness"), niĝ₂-gig DN = תּוֹעֲבַת DN, kal = יָקָר, lu₂-kur₂ = אִישׁ נָכְרִי, zid (of persons) = אִישׁ אֱמֶת, si sa₂ = יֹשֶׁר, ḫu-ru-um = נִבְעָר (כְּסִיל only lil₂), zeb = עָרֵב, ku₇ = מָתוֹק, ḫi-li = חֵן, gu₂ = צַוָּאר (with runs 5–6), gu₂ šub = הִשְׁלִיךְ צַוָּאר; the formula of 1.152–1.153 and 3.9 is giri₁₇-zal-še₃ nu-il₂ לְשָׂשׂוֹן – לֹא נָשָׂא (not ezen nu-tuku). Letters: אֶל X אֱמֹר: / זֶה אֲשֶׁר Y אוֹמֵר: / הוֹסֵף: / מַבּוּל הוּא!; giĝ₄ / ma-na / gun₂ / sila₃ = שֶׁקֶל / מָנֶה / כִּכָּר / קַב; mu sa₄ = קָרָא שֵׁם (= nabû). False friends and traps: ברוך "gently" and היינו "we were" trip the blessing and wine gates; שבו / שבה "in it" the שוב gate; לשאול contains שאול; מגן contains גן; לא יכלה "could not" / "will perish" (vocalize יָכְלָה); אַגָּן, אַפִּרְיוֹן, מְאוֹרוֹת, הבורא would each import a Bible verse the tablet does not have.

§5.2, lessons (one line each):

  • ★ Write the transliteration as `@` and let the tool fill it from the base text: retyped lines differed from the base twice in the first texts, never after. [everyday voices]
  • ★ Never write a Bible quotation, even "not as a quotation", before printing the verse: every such note in this run had to be redone, and one was wrong (לְכָה נָּא for לֶךְ נָא, Gen 37:14); and write the reference in parentheses after the quotation (`…` (Book ch:v)), because the checker does not see `…`, Book ch:v (17 such quotations had gone unchecked). [everyday voices]
  • Anchor every gate at word start and end, and test it on the commonest Hebrew words of the genre: שבו, היינו, ברוך, מגן, לפתיתי, שבה all tripped unanchored or one-letter-prefix gates. [everyday voices]
  • A pre-set formula can be wrong: the renderings had ezen nu-tuku for proverbs 1.152–153 from the literature; the tablets have giri₁₇-zal-še₃ nu-il₂. Check every pre-set formula against the transliteration of its first occurrence. [everyday voices]
  • One Sumerian word, its Akkadian equivalent's Hebrew – unless the Sumerian is wider: ḫi-li (= kuzbu עֲגָבִים) describes a mother's charm in 5.5.1, so it took חֵן; record such splits. [everyday voices]

§6.5 names (new in this corpus; vocalized at first occurrence): Nanaya נַנָּיָה, Muʾati מוּאָתִי, Rīm-Sîn רִים־★סִין, Abī-ešuḫ אֲבִי־אֶשׁוּחַ, Ammī-ditāna עַמִּי־דִּיתָנָה, Ammī-ṣaduqa עַמִּי־צָדוּקָה, Šū-Sîn שׁוּ־★סִין, Išḫara אִשְׁחַרָה, Lu-diĝira לוּ־דִּינְגִּירָה, Šat-Eštar שַׁת־אֶשְׁתַּר, Nintinuga נִין־תִּין־אוּגָּה, Ninimma נִין־אִימָּה, Inim-Inana אִינִים־★אִינַנָּה, Inanaka אִינַנָּקָה; Marḫaši מַרְחַשִׁי, Dilmun דִּלְמוּן, Zabalam זַבַּלַם, Larsa לַרְסָה, Susa שׁוּשַׁן, Tigris חִדֶּקֶל.

Names and terms shared with runs 5–6 (looked up on their folders; the lead harmonizes): Belili בֵּלִילִי ★ and Dumuzi דּוּמוּזִי (adopted from run 5); Inana אִינַנָּה ★, Utu אוּתוּ ★, An אַן ★, Enki, Enlil, Nanna נַנָּה, Nisaba נִיסַבָּה, Uruk אוּרוּךְ, Kulaba כּוּלַבָּה, Eridug אֶרִידוּ, Urim אוּר ★ (same as theirs); gu₂ = צַוָּאר and taškarin / taskarinnu = תְּאַשּׁוּר (adopted from run 5); kur (netherworld) = הָאָרֶץ (run 5); lamma = אֵלַת־(הַ)מָּגֵן (same). Splits for the lead: za-gin₃ = לָזוּרִית here (Gilgameš uqnû, LAOS 4 26, 5.5.1 30) but סַפִּיר in runs 5 and 6; en₃-du = זֶמֶר here, זִמְרָה in run 6; guru₇ = אָסָם here (1.146), כְּרִי in run 6; ĝen imperative = בּוֹא here (2.69) – run 6 may differ.

4. History

For history.md, "Learned on …":

  • Learned on the everyday voices (2026-10-21, round 2, run 7: OB love lyrics 835 lines, Sumerian proverbs 500 lines, Sumerian letters 178 lines): the coordinator had no sub-agent tool and translated all three projects itself, text by text in the priority order, with three review passes per project (the first a read-through of every > line beside the normalization, the second by script – a key-lemma check and verify – the third on echo control and quotations). Sources: ORACC AkkLove (CC0, Wasserman's LAOS 4 with translations in the HTML view) replaced the planned SEAL pages; ETCSL 6.1.01–03 with ORACC Q-composites for the proverbs; ETCSL 5.5.1 and eight 3.3.x letters. The OB Akkadian letters (AbB) were not obtained (CDLI 503 all day). Findings: the Old Akkadian Kiš incantation's "to the garden you came down" and its adjuration "until …" (Song 6:2; 2:7); dādūka ṭābū (Song 1:2); proverb 1.8 = Prov 25:17 (kal = הֹקַר), 1.9 = Qoh 6:2 (אִישׁ נָכְרִי יֹאכְלֶנּוּ), 2.20 = Prov 20:4, 2.27 = Qoh 9:16, 3.134 = Ps 23; Lu-diĝira's mother described with the Song's wasf images and the "woman of valour". Slips caught: two retyped transliterations (then the @ + fill workflow), seventeen quotations in an unchecked format and several written from memory (one wrong), a dozen gate collisions (שבו, היינו, ברוך, מגן, לשאול), the aḫāzu / ṣabātu collision (both אחז), a pre-set formula that the tablets do not have (ezen nu-tuku).

Changelog line: 2026-10-21 – Round 2, run 7 (everyday voices): §6.7 bullet for קולות-היום-יום/renderings.md; §5.2 lessons on @-filling, quoting before printing, gate anchoring, checking pre-set formulas, wider Sumerian words; §6.5 names; sources-registry §4 (AkkLove, ETCSL 6.1.01–03, 5.5.1, 3.3.x, the Q-composites); tools.md (kol_tools.py, build_parallels_index.py).

6. Limits

  • No Agent (sub-agent) tool was available to this coordinator: the "translator chain" was run by the coordinator itself, one range after another, each with the written translator brief applied; the review passes were also the coordinator's (partly script-assisted). No quota, rate limit, HTTP 429 or "session limit" was met.
  • CDLI (cdli.earth) answered HTTP 503 from 15:00 (2026-10-21) on (a background probe ran until its time limit).
  • Push: every git push origin main was rejected (non-fast-forward: the user rewrote origin/main's history, moving docs/ to its own branch). As instructed by the brief (no pull / rebase in the shared checkout) the commits stayed local; the lead replays them onto the new origin/main and pushes them (the lead's message: commits up to 943a4ee4 were already on origin). Pushing was stopped on the lead's instruction.

7. Report

Translated and verified: 1,513 lines in three projects, all first drafts, each with three review passes.

  • Project 1, 1-שירי-אהבה/ – all 25 OB / Old Akkadian love texts with an open base text (ORACC AkkLove = LAOS 4): the divine love songs of Nanaya and Muʾati for Abī-ešuḫ (10), the New-Year song for Rīm-Sîn (15), the dialogues "the faithful lover" (16, with its duplicate 04) and "like an apple of its season" (01), the Ištar–Dumuzi song (07), the irtum series for Ammī-ditāna (06), the Kiš songs (13, 14a–f), the bawdy dialogue (18), the shorter 02, 03, 05, 17, and the love incantations (22 Old Akkadian; 20, 23–26 OB). 835 lines in 16 annotated files; translation.rtl.md (20 footnotes).
  • Project 2, 2-משלים-שומריים/ – Sumerian proverb collection 1 complete (194 proverbs, 348 lines) and 83 proverbs (152 lines) from collections 2 and 3, chosen for daily life and for their biblical parallels. 500 lines in 5 files; translation.rtl.md.
  • Project 3, 3-מכתבים/ – the Message of Lu-diĝira to his mother (57 lines) and eight Sumerian letters of private life (121 lines).
  • Checks: kol_tools.py verify LOVE PROV LET OK (coverage, transliteration = base, reserved/gated strings, name traps, formulas, translation = > lines); check_bible_quotes.py 0 problems on every annotated file; parallels-index.md generated (492 rows: Song of Songs 180, Proverbs 67, Genesis 57, Psalms 41, Qohelet 20); print stubs הדפסה/קולות-היום-יום/1-שירי-אהבה.rtl.md, 2-משלים-שומריים.rtl.md, 3-מכתבים.rtl.md.

Key findings for the Bible (details: parallels-index.md, key findings 1–20): the Old Akkadian incantation from Kiš has "to the garden you came down … you came down to the garden" (Song 6:2, 6:11) and an adjuration "I adjure you … until … – you shall not rest" with the frame of Song 2:7 / 5:8, sworn by Ištar and Išḫara where the Song swears by gazelles; dādūka ṭābū "your love-making is good" (Song 1:2) and the Kiš wasf's sissinnu (the Song's hapax סַנְסִנָּיו); the reversed counsel of father and mother in a love charm (Prov 1:8). Proverb 1.8 is Prov 25:17 (הֹקַר רַגְלְךָ, the same verb kal), 1.9 is Qoh 6:2 (אִישׁ נָכְרִי יֹאכְלֶנּוּ), 2.20 is Prov 20:4, 2.27 is Qoh 9:16, 3.176 is Qoh 9:2, 3.118 puts the false witness among the gods' "abominations" as Prov 6:16–19 does, and 3.134 calls the personal god a shepherd who finds pasture (Ps 23). Lu-diĝira describes his mother with the Song's wasf images and with the virtues of the "woman of valour" (Prov 31), and his message ends like Joseph's "your son … is alive" (Gen 45:9, 26); the sick woman's letter-prayer has the friends who stand far off (Ps 38:12), the vow to serve in the temple court (Ps 84:11) and "I will call your name" (Ps 116:13); Gudea is "like sheep without a shepherd" (Num 27:17); Ur-saga's "let no one take my father's house" is Naboth's plea (1 Kgs 21:3).

The ancient mind: love as a force one "seizes" and "casts" (the incantations), sung at court where the king is the goddess's lover, and voiced by women who plead, reject, mock and forgive; the proverbs' world of bread and salt, the poor man nobody greets, the fox's boasting, the scribe who knows no Sumerian, the curse that breeds curses, the girl who chooses her husband, the mother cooling the soup with her mouth; the letters' homesick boy who complains that the bread and beer are stale, the son who cannot look after his mother, the sick woman whose friends stay away, the teacher who sends a pupil silver and clothes – and ends, like every urgent letter, "it is a flood!".

Open decisions for the user (in each project.md, and §5 above): niĝ₂-gig / an-zil both תּוֹעֵבָה; ṣabātu תָּפַס vs Gilgameš אָחַז; za-gin₃ לָזוּרִית vs סַפִּיר; ḫi-li חֵן; šiptu קֶסֶם; māru בֵּן vs יַקִּיר; irimmu חֲרוּז; sukannīnu תּוֹר; gu₂ צַוָּאר shared with ṣawāru.

Skipped or failed: the OB Akkadian private letters (AbB) – CDLI 503 all day, Archibab not on the allowlist; the MB/MA love texts and the Isin incantation tablet (outside the brief's "OB" or not in the export). The run had no sub-agents; all pushes were rejected (local commits, replayed by the lead).
